title: Grateful Dead Live at San Diego International Sports Arena on 1973-11-14
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v7.02 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording with crisp Charlie Miller transfer captures a high‑energy fall ’73 show highlighted by a smoking Here Comes Sunshine and an epic Truckin’ → Other One → Eyes sequence.
ai_review.review: The November 1973 performance shines thanks to a superb soundboard capture that’s clear, balanced, and benefited from the Charlie Miller upgrade. Musically the night is dominated by a monster second set—Truckin’, multiple Other One reprises, Eyes of the World, Wharf Rat and an inspired Here Comes Sunshine—though a few listeners note a minor flub on the HCS ending and occasional first‑set lulls. Overall the band is tight, energetic, and the recording makes every nuance audible.

ai_rating.rationale: 23 reviews overwhelmingly positive (16×5★, 6×4★, 1×3★) give an average of ~4.65; strong show performance and excellent soundboard quality push the weighted rating to about 4.7.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced SBD capture with Charlie Miller's upgrade; occasional minor flub on Here Comes Sunshine ending but overall pristine and highly listenable.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Here Comes Sunshine (ending flub noted by some listeners)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid but occasionally pedestrian; second set flows spectacularly with a Truckin' → Other One → Eyes sandwich, big River sandwich and a soaring Wharf Rat, delivering an extended jazzy jam marathon.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for tight lead guitar, strong vocals on Sugaree and HCS, inventive noodling during jams, occasional lyric slip noted but overall stellar.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as “raging” with powerful bass bombs by some; a few reviewers note moments where he seemed absent or less intense in the second set, but overall his contribution is highlighted as a key driver of the sound.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for a lyric slip in the first verse of HCS and occasional vocal passion; otherwise solid rhythm guitar work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano receives glowing remarks – described as monstrous, “sooo good,” using wah effects, and providing strong melodic support throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s syncopated off‑beat drumming is highlighted as a highlight; Billy (Bobby) Cox’s kit work praised for creative, jazzy contributions.
